acceptance: A request under another account's lease, or an obsolete lease of the same account, is refused as a changed session before it is sent and before any refresh; a lease survives a same-account token refresh. Twenty concurrent requests share one refresh and one business initialization, and twenty concurrent 401s from the old token reuse one new token; the saved sign-in holds only the refresh credential and nothing public holds a token. A network failure while refreshing keeps the credential and the account offline; a refused (401) refresh signs out and clears it; a 403 answer is the account's: it is neither refreshed nor signed out.

Cancelling an authenticated request that is still waiting for its answer ends it at once as cancelled. The managed inference stream is sent by the app with the bearer, the request id as both idempotency key and request id, no redirects, sent once; a change of account ends the open stream.

The app owns the browser sign-in: the login page gets no verifier or token, a callback is exchanged once (a replay and a concurrent duplicate are refused), and no Cloud handoff route is used. Asking again shows the same page of the same pending attempt, which still finishes. A pending sign-in expires (signed out, its browser actions retired) and its listener closes. A wrong host, origin or state is refused without consuming the attempt. A sign-in cut short cannot adopt a late answer. Signing out always completes locally even when remote revocation is unavailable, and a late result of the old generation is refused.

A request still in flight when the session changes is never sent again: a read ends as a changed session and a mutation as an unknown outcome, whatever account signs in next, and a renewal for another account ends the old lease instead of retargeting it.

reason: When the same account signs in again while a request is in flight, TS replays it once under the new session if it is a read-only repository-context POST or a mutation with a canonical idempotency key. The native broker ends the old lease instead: the read reports a changed session and the mutation an unknown outcome, so the caller has to ask again.

acceptance: A template download is sent as the signed-in account only to the store's fixed origin, once more with a renewed session when the store refuses the first, keeping the same lease; signed out, nothing is sent; a malformed template or release id is refused before anything is sent; the store's own requests carry no credential and follow no redirect.

The sign-in result page has the whole copy in all eight Desktop languages, renders each success heading from the browser's language with the app's language first, and has a distinct localized failure without the return form when the app did not complete the sign-in. It is self-contained (no script or image; only inline style, the embedded font, the form and the return frame are allowed; no-store). The listener binds loopback, forwards only the exact callback path and state, answers a replayed callback as used, and returns the app to the front only on the one-time POST.

reason: TS's result page runs a nonce'd script that reveals a puppyone:// launch link when returning to the app fails. The native page is deliberately script-free (its policy allows no script): the return button POSTs to the listener, which stays for 10 minutes, and no launch fallback is drawn (recorded as an intentional difference in Loopback Callback).

acceptance: The hosted Git secret reaches Git only through a secure credential helper (never on a command line, never to a shell or path helper); an inherited plaintext or unknown helper is reset for the canonical URL only; a credential the helper cannot read back fails closed and the person's prior remote and helper values are restored.
